method: Multi-source historical reconciliation; later territorial configurations are not back-projected to 1326-04-07.

anchors.name: Larende/Karaman
anchors.note: Karamanid political core; XIV c. first half is poorly documented, so exact outer frontier remains unresolved.

anchors.name: Ereğli
anchors.note: TDV records Karamanid rule from 1276, destruction by Geyhatu in 1291, and later Karamanid association; no sufficiently precise 7 Apr 1326 boundary evidence found.

anchors.name: Niğde
anchors.control: unresolved; Ilkhanid administrative sphere stronger than later Karamanid configuration
anchors.note: Later sources clearly place Niğde in Karamanid territory, but that configuration cannot be safely projected backward to 1326. Eretna control is documented by Ibn Battuta only in 1332-33, after the scenario date.

anchors.name: Aksaray
anchors.note: The 1332 Ibn Battuta testimony places Aksaray under the Iraqi/Ilkhanid ruler via Eretna's deputy; this is post-1326 evidence, so it is a bracket rather than direct start-date proof. Later claims of Karamanid control are not back-projected.

anchors.name: Kayseri
anchors.confidence: high for broader sphere, medium for exact 1326 local control
anchors.note: Ibn Battuta in 1332-33 describes Kayseri as under the Iraqi ruler, with Iraqi troops and Eretna's household present. Eretna's independent polity belongs to the later 1340s; do not label 1326 as an Eretna state.

chronologyGuards: Do not use the 1380 Karamanid territorial list as a 1326 polygon.
Do not assign Aksaray, Niğde, or Kayseri to the later Eretna state in 1326.
Do not treat the later Karamanid control of Niğde/Aksaray/Kayseri as proof of control on 1326-04-07.
Konya was recovered from the Karamanids by Demirtaş in 1320; therefore the Konya-Karaman frontier must remain separate from the later Karamanid expansion.
Beyşehir, Seydişehir and Akşehir remained Eşrefoğlu territory until the October 9, 1326 death of II Süleyman; subsequent Hamid/Karaman/Sahib Ata partition must not be back-projected to April 7.
networkImplications: Model Larende-Eregli-Konya as a strategic corridor rather than assuming a smooth provincial polygon.
Treat Aksaray-Kayseri as an Ilkhanid administrative/army network layer separate from later Eretna sovereignty.
Keep Niğde as a review-queue node until direct 1326 evidence is found.
Use caravan routes, fortifications, urban anchors and administrative appointments independently from political-control geometry.
